## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sattubhastajātaka* (Ja 402), translated as *The Sack of Flour*, is a canonical narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. Set during the reign of King Janaka of Benares, the tale opens with the verse phrase *Vibbhantacitto ti* [Fausböll 1883]. The Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at Jetavana with reference to the Perfection of Wisdom (*paññāpāramī*); the introductory incident of the present (*paccuppannavatthu*) is cross-referenced to the *Ummaggajātaka* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883].
The story serves as an illustration of the Bodhisatta fulfilling the Perfection of Wisdom during his past existence as Senakapaṇḍita [Mein Da 2015]. In the story, the Bodhisatta demonstrates his discernment by saving an old brahmin from a venomous snake that had crawled inside the brahmin's meal bag [Mein Da 2015]. The wider narrative context involves an old brahmin's young wife plotting to kill him to be with her lover, a tale cited in modern scholarship as exemplifying negative depictions of women in Jātaka literature [Cheng 2007; Mein Da 2015]. In the concluding identification of births (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains that the brahmin was Ānanda, the deity was Sāriputta, and Senakapaṇḍita was the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883].
SuttaCentral registers four modern translations of the text in four languages but lists no direct cross-tradition parallels [SuttaCentral]. Automatically generated alignments by DharmaNexus report nineteen Pali-internal text-reuse matches with the third and fourth volumes of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (such as a shared segment spanning §6.3–7.3 with 94% similarity), primarily reflecting the close correspondence between canonical verses and their commentary, with no cross-language parallels meeting reporting thresholds [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§6.3–7.3 ↔ §3172–3175); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Catuttho bhāgo) (Atk S0513a4) (§1.1–1.4 ↔ §4791–4792)
